title: Ops Atelier: taskflow library for safe admin automation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Support engineers spend time composing ad-hoc shell+API steps for operator tasks. We need a reusable, safe taskflow library (Ops Atelier) that lets us publish typed admin utilities and runbooks-as-tasks which can be executed interactively or scheduled. Goals: 1) Provide parameterized task templates (e.g., rotate-key, node-drain, model-fallback-rollout) with input validation and RBAC context; 2) Integrate audit logging and platform-level policy checks before/after steps; 3) Provide a sandbox 'dry-run' simulation mode that estimates downstream effects and tokenized cost; 4) Emit structured telemetry (per-step latency, errors, feature flags used) to the Console for postmortem and regression monitoring.
scope_in:
- Implement task template registry (yaml/JSON) with schema validation.
- Runtime that executes steps (k8s, cloud APIs, infra-ctl, internal admin RPCs) with per-step retries and idempotency tokens.
- Hooks for audit log write, change set preview, and automatic rollback markers.
- UX: lightweight CLI + Console integration to browse, parameterize, and run tasks.
scope_out:
- Not implementing full workflow orchestration (long-running multi-approval flows) in this phase.
- Not replacing incident runbooks in PagerDuty; we will integrate with PagerDuty links but not own incident lifecycle yet.
proposal_summary: Build a Go-based task runtime that loads typed templates from a git-backed registry (repo or internal store). Each template has a JSON schema for inputs, step definitions, preconditions, and postchecks. The runtime executes steps with a sandbox flag to simulate side effects, captures diffs to an immutable change set, writes an audit event to the central audit service, and emits metrics to the Console. RBAC will be enforced by consulting the platform authz layer before execution. A minimal UI in Console will let SREs preview change sets and run tasks with optional 'require-2fa' guard for high-impact actions.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use typed templates + JSON schema vs freeform scripts: typed templates reduce accidental unsafe commands and enable UI parameterization, at the cost of initial template authoring overhead.
- Git-backed registry vs DB: git gives history and easy PR reviews (favored), DB would be faster for authoring but loses innate code review flow.
- Inline step runners vs external actions: prefer modular runners that call small connector binaries to limit runtime privileges.
- Simulation accuracy: dry-run will be best-effort and may not account for race conditions; we will label sims as non-authoritative and require confirm to run.
acceptance_criteria: A typed task template can be authored in the registry and validated by JSON schema
A user in Console can preview a task with resolved parameters and a generated change set diff
Task execution writes an immutable audit event with input snapshot and step outcomes
Dry-run mode produces an estimated change set and a risk score visible in the UI
Per-step telemetry (latency, error, retries) appears in Console traces and dashboard
RBAC checks prevent execution when the caller lacks required role; system returns clear denial reason
notes: 2026-02-22: Spike complete for git-backed template loader. Prototype loads templates from a private repo and validates schema locally.
2026-03-01: Security reviewed prototype approach; requested HSM/KMS integration for any key-rotation steps and confirmation flow for high-privilege actions.
2026-03-04: Decided to implement per-step idempotency tokens to support safe retries after transient failures.
2026-03-10: Start integrating audit events with central audit service; schema for audit event agreed with security team (audit_v2).
